questions.text: What is a chemical reaction?
options: A process where reactants change into new products with different properties
A physical change like melting ice
questions.correct: A process where reactants change into new products with different properties

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a sign that a chemical reaction has occurred?
options: Change in shape only, without any other change
questions.correct: Change in shape only, without any other change

questions.text: Hydrogen peroxide (H₂O₂) breaking into water and oxygen is an example of:
questions.correct: Decomposition

questions.text: Vinegar + baking soda producing fizzing is an example of:
questions.correct: Acid on carbonate

questions.text: What gas is released when an acid reacts with a metal?
questions.correct: Hydrogen (H₂)

questions.text: Burning LPG in a stove is an example of:
questions.correct: Combustion

questions.text: What are the products of complete combustion of a hydrocarbon fuel?
questions.correct: Carbon dioxide and water

questions.text: Why should you NEVER mix bleach with ammonia cleaner?
options: It releases toxic chloramine gas that can damage lungs
questions.correct: It releases toxic chloramine gas that can damage lungs

questions.text: Which equation correctly represents photosynthesis?
questions.correct: 6CO₂ + 6H₂O + light → C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂

questions.text: Which equation correctly represents cellular respiration?
questions.correct: C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂ → 6CO₂ + 6H₂O + energy (ATP)

questions.text: Why must a chemical equation be balanced?
options: Because of the Law of Conservation of Mass — atoms are neither created nor destroyed
questions.correct: Because of the Law of Conservation of Mass — atoms are neither created nor destroyed

questions.text: Where in the cell does cellular respiration mainly occur?
questions.correct: Mitochondria

questions.text: What is ATP?
options: The energy currency of the cell — used for cellular work
questions.correct: The energy currency of the cell — used for cellular work

questions.text: Why are photosynthesis and respiration considered 'opposite reactions'?
options: Their reactants and products are reversed
They happen in the same organelle
questions.correct: Their reactants and products are reversed

questions.text: Balance this equation: __ H₂ + O₂ → __ H₂O. What are the correct coefficients?
questions.correct: 2 and 2

questions.text: What is a solution?
options: A homogeneous mixture of two or more substances
A heterogeneous mixture where particles settle at the bottom
questions.correct: A homogeneous mixture of two or more substances

questions.text: In saltwater, which is the solvent?
questions.correct: Water

questions.text: Why is water called the 'universal solvent'?
options: It dissolves more substances than any other liquid
It is denser than other liquids
questions.correct: It dissolves more substances than any other liquid

questions.text: Soda is what type of solution?
questions.correct: Gas-in-liquid

questions.text: Air is best described as which type of solution?
questions.correct: Gas-in-gas

questions.text: What is saturation?
options: The point where no more solute can dissolve in a solvent at a given temperature
When a solution is diluted with water
questions.correct: The point where no more solute can dissolve in a solvent at a given temperature

questions.text: What happens to a plant in soil with very high salt concentration?
options: Water moves out of the plant roots due to osmotic stress, causing wilting
It grows faster because salt is a nutrient
questions.correct: Water moves out of the plant roots due to osmotic stress, causing wilting

questions.text: What is saltwater intrusion?
options: Seawater seeping into freshwater aquifers, making them salty and unusable
Adding salt to freshwater for drinking
questions.correct: Seawater seeping into freshwater aquifers, making them salty and unusable

questions.text: What does the GHS skull-and-crossbones symbol mean?
options: Acute toxicity — can cause death or serious harm
questions.correct: Acute toxicity — can cause death or serious harm

questions.text: Which GHS symbol warns that a chemical can corrode skin or metals?
questions.correct: Corrosion (test tube dripping on surface)

questions.text: Why must acids and bases be stored separately?
options: They can react violently if they touch
questions.correct: They can react violently if they touch

questions.text: What is the BEST way to dispose of leftover household chemicals?
options: Take them to a designated hazardous waste collection point following DENR guidelines
Pour them into the storm drain
Throw them in the regular trash
questions.correct: Take them to a designated hazardous waste collection point following DENR guidelines

questions.text: What is eutrophication?
options: Algal blooms caused by excess nutrients (phosphates) in water — kills fish
questions.correct: Algal blooms caused by excess nutrients (phosphates) in water — kills fish

questions.text: Which Philippine law specifically regulates toxic substances and hazardous waste?
Why is proper chemical disposal important?
options: To protect aquatic ecosystems, prevent water contamination, and keep drinking water safe
To increase the volume of the ocean
questions.correct: To protect aquatic ecosystems, prevent water contamination, and keep drinking water safe

questions.text: What is the basic structural and functional unit of all living things?
questions.correct: The cell

questions.text: Which theme of life science explains why you sweat when it's hot?
questions.correct: Homeostasis

questions.text: Which of the following correctly orders levels of biological organization from SIMPLEST to MOST COMPLEX?
options: Cell → Tissue → Organ → Organ System → Organism
questions.correct: Cell → Tissue → Organ → Organ System → Organism

questions.text: Which statement BEST describes the structure-function relationship?
options: The shape of a biological part determines what job it can perform
Function is random and unrelated to structure
questions.correct: The shape of a biological part determines what job it can perform

questions.text: Why are alveoli in the lungs so tiny and numerous?
options: To create a huge surface area for gas exchange
To make them easier to see
questions.correct: To create a huge surface area for gas exchange

questions.text: Which organelle is known as the 'powerhouse of the cell'?
questions.correct: Mitochondria

questions.text: Which process moves molecules from LOW to HIGH concentration, using energy (ATP)?
questions.correct: Active transport

questions.text: A potato slice placed in salty water becomes soft and shriveled. Why?
options: Water left the potato cells by osmosis because the salt solution had lower water concentration
Salt destroyed the potato cells chemically
questions.correct: Water left the potato cells by osmosis because the salt solution had lower water concentration

questions.text: Which organelle performs photosynthesis in plant cells?
questions.correct: Chloroplast

questions.text: Which plant organ is primarily responsible for absorbing water and minerals?
questions.correct: Roots

questions.text: Which vascular tissue transports water upward from roots to leaves?
questions.correct: Xylem

questions.text: Which vascular tissue transports sugar (food) throughout the plant?
questions.correct: Phloem

questions.text: What is transpiration?
options: Loss of water vapor from leaves through stomata
Absorption of minerals by the roots
questions.correct: Loss of water vapor from leaves through stomata

questions.text: Why does removing a complete ring of bark kill a tree?
options: It cuts the phloem, so sugars cannot reach the roots, which then starve and die
It removes the tree's protective armor
questions.correct: It cuts the phloem, so sugars cannot reach the roots, which then starve and die

questions.text: Which brain region coordinates body temperature?
questions.correct: Hypothalamus

questions.text: What is the 1st line of defense against pathogens?
options: Physical barriers like skin and mucous membranes
questions.correct: Physical barriers like skin and mucous membranes

questions.text: How do vaccines protect you from future infections?
options: They create memory B and T cells that respond quickly if the real pathogen appears
They kill all pathogens in your body permanently
They cause the disease in a mild form only
questions.correct: They create memory B and T cells that respond quickly if the real pathogen appears

questions.text: Which BEST describes the difference between nervous and endocrine responses?
options: Nervous is fast and short-term; endocrine is slower but longer-lasting
Nervous is slow; endocrine is fast
questions.correct: Nervous is fast and short-term; endocrine is slower but longer-lasting

questions.text: A torn ACL affects which body part?
questions.correct: The knee joint

questions.text: Which of the following is a symptom of an asthma attack?
options: Difficulty breathing and wheezing due to narrowed bronchioles
questions.correct: Difficulty breathing and wheezing due to narrowed bronchioles

questions.text: What is the difference between weather and climate?
options: Weather is short-term; climate is long-term
Weather is long-term; climate is short-term
questions.correct: Weather is short-term; climate is long-term

questions.text: What is the MAIN cause of recent climate change?
options: Human activities releasing greenhouse gases like CO₂ and methane
questions.correct: Human activities releasing greenhouse gases like CO₂ and methane

questions.text: What happens to corals when water temperature rises too much?
options: They expel their symbiotic algae and bleach, slowly starving
questions.correct: They expel their symbiotic algae and bleach, slowly starving

questions.text: Which of the following is a BIOLOGICAL response to climate change?
options: Species shifting to cooler areas (range shift)
questions.correct: Species shifting to cooler areas (range shift)

questions.text: Why is the Philippines highly vulnerable to climate change?
options: It's an archipelago in the typhoon belt with thousands of coastal communities
It's located far from the ocean
questions.correct: It's an archipelago in the typhoon belt with thousands of coastal communities

questions.text: What is the difference between adaptation and mitigation?
options: Adaptation adjusts to climate impacts; mitigation reduces the causes of climate change
Adaptation reduces emissions; mitigation adjusts to impacts
questions.correct: Adaptation adjusts to climate impacts; mitigation reduces the causes of climate change

questions.text: Which of the following is an example of MITIGATION?
options: Switching to solar energy to reduce fossil fuel use
questions.correct: Switching to solar energy to reduce fossil fuel use

questions.text: Which Philippine law created the Climate Change Commission?
How does overpopulation affect the environment?
options: It increases resource demand, deforestation, waste, and greenhouse gas emissions
It only affects cities, not farms
questions.correct: It increases resource demand, deforestation, waste, and greenhouse gas emissions

questions.text: Which of the following BEST summarizes the main idea of Term 2?
options: Chemistry and life science principles interact — chemical reactions shape environments, and biological systems maintain life through coordination and defense
Only chemistry matters in daily life
Only biology matters in daily life
Neither chemistry nor biology is important
questions.correct: Chemistry and life science principles interact — chemical reactions shape environments, and biological systems maintain life through coordination and defense
